1	# WP-001: Build filter/sort toolbar DOM and CSS
     2	
     3	## Description
     4	
     5	Create the filter/sort toolbar UI component for the project list dashboard, including a search input, repository filter dropdown, and sort selector, with appropriate CSS styling.
     6	
     7	## Scope
     8	
     9	- `gui/public/js/views/dashboard.js` — add `buildFilterToolbar()` function, fetch `api.repositories.list()` in `renderDashboard()`, insert toolbar between page header and project list container
    10	- `gui/public/css/styles.css` — add `.project-filter-toolbar` styles and related selectors
    11	
    12	## Dependencies
    13	
    14	- None
    15	
    16	## Acceptance Criteria
    17	
    18	1. The dashboard renders a visible filter toolbar between the page header and the project list.
    19	2. The toolbar contains a search input with placeholder "Search projects…" and `type="search"`.
    20	3. The toolbar contains a repository filter `<select>` with an "All repositories" default option and one option per registered repository (value = repo ID, label = repo Name).
    21	4. The toolbar contains a sort selector `<select>` with "Alphabetical" (value `alpha`, default) and "Last Activity" (value `activity`) options.
    22	5. If `api.repositories.list()` fails, the toolbar still renders with search and sort controls (no repository dropdown), and a toast error message is shown.
    23	6. The toolbar's CSS layout follows the flex pattern established by `.error-log-filter-bar`.
    24	7. DOM clearing uses `clearElement()` from `utils/dom.js` — no `innerHTML = ''` for container clearing.
    25	8. All three controls fire an `onFilterChange()` callback with the current filter/sort state when their values change. The search input uses a debounced `input` event (~250ms).
    26	
    27	## Active Pipeline Stages
    28	
    29	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`

1	# WP-002: Extend ProjectData with LastActivity and add updateLastActivity()
     2	
     3	## Description
     4	
     5	Add an optional `LastActivity` field to the `ProjectData` interface and implement an `updateLastActivity()` method on `ProjectManager` that persists the value without modifying `DateModified`.
     6	
     7	## Scope
     8	
     9	- `src/models/project/project.types.ts` — add `LastActivity?: string` to `ProjectData` interface
    10	- `src/models/project/project.manager.ts` — add `updateLastActivity()` public method
    11	- `src/tests/project.manager.test.ts` — add unit tests for `updateLastActivity()`
    12	
    13	## Dependencies
    14	
    15	- None
    16	
    17	## Acceptance Criteria
    18	
    19	1. `ProjectData` interface in `project.types.ts` includes `LastActivity?: string` as an optional field.
    20	2. `updateLastActivity()` sets `LastActivity` on the project JSON file and does NOT modify `DateModified`.
    21	3. `updateLastActivity()` short-circuits without writing to disk when the new value equals the existing `LastActivity` value.
    22	4. `updateLastActivity()` silently returns (no error thrown) when called with a project ID that does not exist.

    24	6. New unit tests in `project.manager.test.ts` verify all four behaviours above.
